title: General John Stark's Report on the Battle of Bennington to General Schuyler, Aug[ust 1777]
issues: URL memory.loc.gov/ammem/amlaw/lwcc.html returned HTTP 403 Forbidden.

Historical note: Stark's primary report after Bennington (August 22, 1777) was addressed to the New Hampshire Committee of Safety and to General Lincoln, not directly to General Schuyler. Attribution to Schuyler warrants further verification; a report through Schuyler's command may exist as a forwarded document in PCC but the addressee in the title appears inaccurate.
Title specificity cannot be confirmed at this collection-level URL.

title: Journals of the Continental Congress: Vermont Statehood Debates, 1777-1791
issues: URL memory.loc.gov/ammem/amlaw/lwjc.html returned HTTP 403 Forbidden.
Even if accessible, the URL is the collection landing page for the full Journals of the Continental Congress (34 volumes), not filtered to Vermont statehood debates.

Factual concern: The Continental Congress ceased to exist in 1789 when the new federal Congress convened. The Journals of the Continental Congress end in 1789; they cannot cover events through 1791. Vermont was admitted to the Union on March 4, 1791, under the new Congress, not the Continental Congress. The date range '1777-1791' in the title is misleading or erroneous for this specific source.
Debates from 1790-1791 on Vermont's admission would appear in the Annals of Congress (First Congress), not the Journals of the Continental Congress.
recommendation: Correct the date range to reflect what the Journals actually cover (through 1788/1789). For Vermont admission debates in 1790-1791, cite the Annals of Congress or Senate records from the First Congress. Provide a specific volume and page reference rather than the collection homepage.
